To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic ventricular MI with minimal or no atrial involvement is associated with increased AF vulnerability that is associated with atrioventricular conduction disturbances, increased biatrial sympathetic hyperinnervation, and heterogeneous alteration of atrioventricular electrical restitution.
hearts with chronic MI exhibit heterogeneous sympathetic hyperinnervation and altered atrial electrical restitution that may contribute to the increased vulnerability for AF.
chronic MI is accompanied by heterogeneous atrial neural and electrophysiological remodeling that may be responsible, at least in part, for the increased AF incidence in this condition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of atrial fibrillations in patients with chronic left ventricle myocardial infarctions.
the mechanisms underlying increased AF vulnerability and AF maintenance in the setting of chronic ventricular MI with normal atrial structure and electrical activity.
the mechanisms of arrhythmias and heart failure, and the development of novel therapeutic strategies to treat these conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic left ventricular MI with or without atrial involvement causes a heterogeneous alteration in the atrial electrical properties, including electrical restitution and atrioventricular conduction.
chronic ventricular MI with or without atrial involvement causes atrial electrical and sympathetic neural remodeling that might provide important substrate for the increased AF vulnerability.
chronic MI causes atrial electrical and neurohumoral remodeling that may provide important substrates and mechanisms for the increased AF vulnerability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic MI causes atrial electrical and autonomic remodeling that might provide important substrate for the increased AF vulnerability.
the atrial electrical and sympathetic neural alterations caused by chronic ventricular MI are important substrates for AF.
we have identified a new substrate for atrial fibrillation in the heart.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chronic MI is a risk factor for AF.
atrial fibrillation is more common in hearts with chronic myocardial infarctions than in normal hearts.
the atria of dogs with chronic left ventricle myocardial infarct have increased susceptibility for atrial fibrillation.
